title: Checkpoint: Birds
objective: After this level you can explain how birds' bodies are built for flight and survival.
summary: A bird's body is a flying machine. The ostrich dropped the flying: no keel, no flight, but fast two-toed feet, the largest living bird and the largest egg of any living bird.

cards.headline: Chapter 3 finale: a bird that traded flying for running.
cards.body: This chapter built a flying machine: feathers, air-filled bones, lift from turned air, and a keel for the flight muscles. Now meet a bird that dropped the flying and kept the rest.

cards.fact: The ostrich is the largest living bird.
cards.context: An adult male may stand 2.75 m tall and weigh more than 150 kg. It lives in open country in Africa, and it cannot fly. Instead, a frightened ostrich can run at about 70 km/h, on the only two-toed feet of any bird, the main toe built almost like a hoof. Its escape plan is its legs.

mascot.line: Two toes, one very fast plan: leave.

cards.headline: No keel, no flight
cards.body: Remember Level 22's keel, the breastbone ridge that anchors the flight muscles? Ostriches, emus and their relatives, the ratites, have a smooth, raftlike breastbone with no keel at all. With nowhere to anchor big flight muscles, they can't fly. Size still counts, though: the ostrich lays the largest egg of any living bird, about 15 cm long.

cards.headline: Chapter 3 complete
learned: Feathers make a bird; big fliers have air-filled bones
Wings lift by turning air; a keel anchors flight muscles
Raptors, owls, penguins, hummingbirds: bodies built for jobs
Record migrants run on fat and steer by sun, stars, magnetism
The ostrich: no keel, no flight, the largest living bird

questions.prompt: Birds recap: which bird is the largest one alive today?

options.label: The emperor penguin
options.rationale: Penguins are big, but the ostrich is larger.

options.label: The frigatebird
options.rationale: Long wings, light skeleton, far smaller body.

options.label: The bald eagle
options.rationale: Eagles build huge nests, but the ostrich is the largest bird.

questions.explanation: The ostrich is the largest living bird; a male may stand 2.75 m tall and weigh more than 150 kg.

questions.prompt: Birds recap: why can't an ostrich fly?

options.label: Its feathers are too heavy
options.rationale: The card points to the breastbone.

options.label: Its wings were lost entirely
options.rationale: It still has wings; it lacks the keel.

options.label: Its breastbone has no keel for flight muscles
Its bones are too hollow
options.rationale: The missing piece is the keel.

questions.explanation: Ratites like the ostrich have a smooth, keel-less breastbone, so there's nowhere to anchor big flight muscles.

questions.prompt: Birds recap: penguins and ostriches both gave up flying through air. What did each do instead?

options.label: Both glide from cliffs
options.rationale: Neither glides; one swims, one runs.

options.label: Penguins swim with flippers; ostriches run

questions.explanation: Penguins turned their wings into flippers for swimming; ostriches run on two-toed feet.

questions.prompt: Birds recap, from Level 29: in the 2010 tracking study, about how far did Arctic terns fly each year?

options.label: About 2.4 million km
options.rationale: That's the estimate for a whole lifetime.

questions.explanation: The 11 tracked terns averaged 70,900 km a year on migration.

questions.prompt: Birds recap, from Level 25: what let a barn owl strike its target in total darkness?

options.label: Eyes that see in complete darkness
A keen sense of smell
options.rationale: The owl struck paper, which ruled out smell.

questions.explanation: Uneven ears let a barn owl locate sounds in three dimensions, so it can strike by sound alone.
